title: Partner tenant onboarding: API contracts and snippet playground
body:
Purpose:
This is a working playground doc for partner tenant onboarding details focused on three interlocking areas: API contracts (trial provisioning, entitlements, deprovision), tile copy & CTA variants for marketplace listings, and the telemetry/event schema we need from partners for post-launch diagnostics.

Context / why this exists:
- We see frequent mismatches between marketplace tile promises (trial available, auto-provisioning) and the partner integration: missing API fields, different auth flows, and insufficient telemetry for debugging.
- This doc captures precise mini-contracts we should ask partners to support, plus short copy permutations for listing tiles and email CTAs that map to technical capabilities.
- Working doc: keep short, actionable, and pragmatic. Not a final legal contract.

Scope (what we aim to cover in 1–2 sprints):
1) Minimal API surface required for self-serve trial provisioning and deprovision.
2) Entitlement model sketch: tenant-scoped entitlements, seat vs consumption flags, and expiration semantics.
3) Marketplace tile copy variants (3 headline x 3 description x 2 CTA tones).
4) Telemetry event list + required attributes (for our console and rollout tracing).
5) Implementation checklist and acceptance gates.

1) Minimal API surface (recommended endpoints + contracts)
Note: assume partner exposes an authenticated partner API over TLS. We prefer OAuth2 client credentials or API tokens; SAML-based backends require extra ops work.

- POST /marketplace/tenants/provision
  - Purpose: create a tenant resource scoped to a Redwood Marketplace purchase or trial.
  - Required fields (body): { "external_customer_id", "requested_tier", "region", "callback_url" }
  - Response: 201 with { "tenant_id", "admin_url", "confirmation_code", "expires_at" }
  - Expected semantics: the confirmation_code serves as a short-lived token the marketplace UI can surface to the customer for immediate confirmation.

- GET /marketplace/tenants/{tenant_id}/status
  - Purpose: polling or webhook target for provisioning state.
  - Response codes: 200 { "state": "ACTIVE|PENDING|FAILED|DELAYED", "details": "human message" }, 404 (not found), 401 (auth).

- POST /marketplace/tenants/{tenant_id}/entitlements
  - Purpose: attach entitlements (trial, seats, consumption budgets).
  - Required fields: { "entitlement_type": "TRIAL|SEAT|CONSUMPTION", "quantity": int, "expires_at": ISO8601|null, "meta": {} }
  - Idempotency: client should support an idempotency-key header; partner should dedupe.

- POST /marketplace/tenants/{tenant_id}/deprovision
  - Purpose: immediate removal of trial tenant resources (on trial end or cancellation).
  - Behavior: best-effort async; return 202 with { "job_id" } and provide /jobs/{job_id} for status.

- Webhook: /marketplace/webhooks (optional but preferred)
  - Events: provisioning.completed, provisioning.failed, entitlements.updated, deprovision.completed
  - Security: HMAC signature header + timestamp; include the public key or secret exchange step.

2) Entitlement model recommendations
- Tenant-scoped primary entity: tenant_id (opaque string). Everything else is child of tenant_id.
- Entitlement types: TRIAL (time-bound), SEAT (concurrent users), CONSUMPTION (credits, tokens).
- Expiration semantics: partner must support an expires_at on entitlement objects and a server-side enforcement path (e.g., returns 403 for API calls post-expiry).
- Grace period policy suggested: 48 hours for trials to reduce churn friction; partners may reject but should document.
- Billing vs trial separation: Trial entitlements must be distinct from paid entitlements; marketplace purchase flow will upgrade the entitlement via entitlements API.

3) Marketplace tile copy & CTA variants (match to technical capabilities)
Guidelines: headline length <= 60 chars, description <= 150 chars. Prefer active verbs. Match CTA to feature parity:
- If partner supports auto-provisioning: CTA = "Start free trial — instant setup"
- If partner requires manual steps: CTA = "Request trial access — we'll follow up"
- If partner supports a fully managed demo: CTA = "Book a demo"

Headline variants (examples):
- "Multi-tenant LLM inference for product teams"
- "Low-latency model serving with predictable throughput"
- "Secure private deployments with VPC and KMS"

Description variants (examples):
- "Start a 14‑day trial and provision a tenant in seconds. Includes dedicated GPU pools and SLA-backed routes."
- "Self-serve API for model inference, auto-scaling, and detailed per-token billing — free trial available."
- "Enterprise-ready deployment options (Hosted, Dedicated, Private) with audit logs and KMS integration."

CTA tone matrix (2 tones):
- Direct: "Start free trial" / "Get started"
- Assisted: "Request trial access" / "Talk to sales"

Mapping table (example):
- auto-provisioning + webhook -> Direct CTA + instant success flow
- manual provisioning -> Assisted CTA + expected SLA note in tile copy

4) Telemetry & event schema (console-friendly minimal set)
We need these events surfaced by partners (or available via our integration read APIs) so the Redwood Console can show rollout health and failures. Event names are suggested; partners may map, but we require the attributes.

Required events and attributes:
- provisioning.requested
  - tenant_id, request_id, external_customer_id, requested_tier, timestamp, initiator (marketplace|partner-ui)
- provisioning.completed
  - tenant_id, request_id, duration_ms, region, result: SUCCESS|FAILURE, error_code|null, timestamp
- entitlement.added
  - tenant_id, entitlement_type, quantity, expires_at|null, actor, timestamp
- entitlement.revoked
  - tenant_id, entitlement_type, reason, actor, timestamp
- deprovision.started
  - tenant_id, job_id, initiated_by, timestamp
- deprovision.completed
  - tenant_id, job_id, duration_ms, success, timestamp

Format guidance:
- JSON payloads, top-level keys as above.
- Timestamp in ISO8601 UTC.
- If using webhooks, include an event_type header and a signature header for verification.

5) Implementation checklist & acceptance gates (short)
- Auth: OAuth2 client credentials or API token documented in partner onboarding doc.
- API: POST /provision responds 201 within 10s for simple tenants (otherwise return PENDING).
- Webhook or polling: provisioning.completed delivered within 5 minutes for 90% of requests.
- Entitlements: partner accepts entitlements API calls idempotently and enforces expires_at semantics.
- Deprovision: job-based async deprovisioning and /jobs endpoint for status.
- Telemetry: at least provisioning.completed and deprovision.completed events within payload retention of 30 days.
- UI/UX: CTA in listing must match provisioning capability (no "instant" claim without auto-provisioning).

Acceptance criteria (go/no-go for listing tile):
- TECH: Partner passes basic smoke tests (provision -> status -> entitlement attach -> deprovision).
- OPS: Partner agrees to sign webhook secret exchange (or provide polling API) and to a support SLA for marketplace customers (response within 24h for provisioning failures during business hours).
- COMMS: Copy finalized and approved by partner and Redwood GTM; CTA mapped correctly.

Rollout sequencing / recommended pilot flow:
1) Private beta with 3 customers: manual provisioning with Redwood SEs; collect telemetry and refine API shape.
2) Pilot: enable auto-provisioning with webhook; limit to 10 customers per week. Monitor provisioning.completed duration and failures.
3) Gradual marketplace listing: open trials to self-serve after 2 weeks with failure rate < 5% and mean provisioning time < 120s.

Notes / open questions (things to resolve with partner):
- Can partner support idempotency keys natively? If not, do we need a mapping layer?
- Are there SSO constraints (SAML-only orgs) that block immediate provisioning?
- What billing metadata do partners need to reconcile marketplace purchases? (invoice_id, sku_code, marketplace_order_id)
- Can partner expose a /jobs endpoint to track long-running deprovision operations?

Copy QA checklist (for GTM)
- Headline <= 60 chars, Description <= 150 chars.
- No absolute claims about latency unless partner provides SLAs. Use qualifiers: "typical p95 latency < 200ms" instead of "sub-200ms latency".
- CTA aligned with technical capability.

Quick PR snips (for partner SDK repo)
- Example: provision call (curl)
  curl -X POST https://api.partner.example/marketplace/tenants/provision \n    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \n    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n    -d '{ "external_customer_id": "redwood-123", "requested_tier": "trial", "region": "us-west-2", "callback_url": "https://marketplace.redwood.ai/callback" }'

- Example webhook verification (python):
  signature = request.headers.get('X-Partner-Sig')
  body = request.data
  expected = hmac_sha256(secret, body)
  if not safe_compare(signature, expected): reject(401)

Appendix: sample short blurbs for tile copy (copy-paste friendly)
- "Start a free 14-day trial. Instant tenant provisioning and clear per-token billing. Get started."
- "Request a trial: we’ll provision a tenant and help migrate your models. Support available via chat."
- "Book a demo to explore Dedicated GPU pools, autoscaling, and enterprise SLAs."

End of doc.
